newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar reiterates taking Bahrain row to World Court.
newsitem.headline: Qatar reiterates taking Bahrain row to World Court.

text.p: Qatar hopes to find a solution to its border row with Bahrain within the framework of a 1990 agreement which forsees taking the case to the World Court, a senior Qatari official said on Thursday.

"The agreement signed by Qatar and Bahrain in 1990 is a valid document and it allows both parties to take the dispute to the International Court of Justice in The Hague, besides giving the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia a chance to mediate", he told Reuters.
The dispute involves a cluster of small islands and sandbanks in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
Doha has filed a case at the International Court of Justice. The move has angered Manama, which demands Qatar withdraw the case in favour of Saudi mediation.
Qatar has said it would withdraw the case only if Saudi mediation resolved the dispute before a verdict from The Hague.

A summit of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates -- held in Doha this month and boycotted by Bahrain decided to set up a committee at Bahrain's request to help ease tensions between the two neighbours.

The committee, comprising the foreign ministers of the other four GCC states, is to hold its first meeting in Cairo on Saturday and try to arrange a "face-to-face encounter" with the foreign ministers of Qatar and Bahrain, said the Qatari official.
"Its brief is to just clear the atmosphere of mistrust and promote understanding between the two countries and not to mediate or try to resolve the territorial dispute," he said.
"The resolution of the dispute has to be found within the framework of the 1990 agreement between the two countries", he added.
Qatar-Bahrain ties have been further strained since Bahrain charged a Qatari man and woman this month with spying for Qatar. A court sentenced the duo to three years in jail on Wednesday.
Qatar denounced the sentences and demanded ther release. It earlier accused Bahrain of plotting to undermine its stability.
